pr.title: Add install.sh and field upgrade: install a checkout and keep it current (install.md chunk 1)
pr.head: 50611d8199aca6eff720086c99b42b9de3d5d7c9

summary: Field is installed from a git checkout, and it has three pieces that each go stale on their own. The field command is TypeScript built into dist/. The audio daemon field-audiod is a C++ binary built with CMake and JUCE. The model workers are Python environments that uv manages. Until this change, installing meant four pnpm commands run inside the checkout, and nothing said which piece was out of date after a git pull.

This pull request adds install.sh at the repository root. It installs the checkout it sits in: it builds the CLI and links it onto your PATH through pnpm, builds the daemon, and re-syncs the worker environments someone already set up. It never sets up a new worker, because that starts a download of several gigabytes. field upgrade [target] runs the same script from any directory, and field upgrade status compares each piece with its source and names the command that fixes it. The installer never pulls and never switches branches, because the checkout may hold work in progress.

Three smaller changes support it. field setup gains --existing and --check, so the CLI, which owns the list of workers, says which are set up. Eight daemon error messages name one build command, BUILD_DAEMON. And pnpm gen:limits stops rewriting an unchanged C++ header, which made the daemon look stale after every test run. On Windows the installer does not run, so field upgrade refuses there and lists the manual steps.

cards.title: What each target runs
cards.html:
TargetRuns
clipnpm install --frozen-lockfile, pnpm run build, then pnpm add -g <checkout> unless pnpm's global field already links this checkout
audiodpnpm run build:native, then touch the binary so audiod-stale clears
workersfield setup --existing from the checkout's dist/
all (default)cli, audiod, then workers
statusOne row per fact, changing nothing

Each target checks every prerequisite it needs before its first command. Every target except status ends by fetching the checkout's upstream and warning when the branch is behind it.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Checkout: the git clone of Field that install.sh sits in, and the code that field runs.
  • The link: pnpm's global node_modules/field, a symlink into the checkout that pnpm add -g <checkout> creates. A new build takes effect without relinking.
  • Build stamp: dist/build-info.json, which pnpm build writes with the commit it built and the number of uncommitted files it saw.
  • Set up: a worker whose console script is installed in python/<worker>/.venv, the test field generate applies before starting one.
  • Upstream: the remote branch that the checkout's branch tracks, @{upstream} in git.

cards.title: What the plan leaves for later
cards.html:
• Chunk 2, releases: prebuilt CLI and daemon archives with checksums, blocked on the license question, because the daemon links JUCE, which is AGPLv3 or commercial.
  • Chunk 3, the release installer: the same install.sh installing a release with only Node 24, curl, and tar.

groups.title: The installer: install.sh
groups.kicker: One bash script installs the checkout it sits in, one target at a time, and reports what is out of date.
intro: install.sh treats itself as a checkout's installer when src/cli.ts sits beside it. Piped from curl, bash reads it from stdin with nothing beside it, and it says to clone instead. A later chunk adds release installs for that case. It is written for bash 3.2, the version macOS ships, and takes one target, all when given none.

Each target checks every prerequisite it needs before its first command: Node 24 or newer, pnpm, pnpm's global bin directory on PATH unless field already links this checkout, and cmake for audiod and all. A missing one stops the installer with exit status 69 and nothing changed.

The cli target keeps the install shape the README already documented. pnpm add -g <checkout> makes pnpm's global field a symlink into the checkout. To tell which checkout pnpm links, linked_checkout reads pnpm ls -g --json and resolves the path it names. A link that already points here is left alone, and one that points at another checkout moves, with a moved row naming both.
status compares each piece with its source:

• Checkout: commits in HEAD..@{upstream} and @{upstream}..HEAD after a fetch, which FIELD_OFFLINE=1 skips. A branch behind its upstream warns, and one only ahead reports repo-ahead.
  • CLI: the build stamp's commit and dirty-file count against the checkout's, the comparison field --version already makes.
  • Daemon: the binary's modification time against every tracked file under native/audiod. The installer touches the binary after each build, because CMake relinks it only when its own inputs change.
  • Workers: the rows field setup --check prints, passed through.

checks.text: Exit statuses: 69 for a missing prerequisite, 64 for an unknown target, and 1 when the daemon build fails. Messages name field upgrade <target> as the way back when pnpm's field links this checkout, and the script's own path otherwise (rerun).

files.note: The whole installer: prerequisite checks, the four install targets, and the status rows.

checks.text: The JSON shape linked_checkout reads matches pnpm 11.15.1: pnpm ls -g --json lists dependencies.field.path as a node_modules/field path in the global directory, which pwd -P resolves to the linked checkout. Checked against a real listing.
require_cmake checks that cmake is on PATH, not its version. The thread on docs/install.md line 33 is about that gap.
Moving the link works with the real pnpm 11.15.1. In a throwaway PNPM_HOME, pnpm add -g of a second package named field replaced the first, and pnpm ls -g --json then named the new path.

This touch is what clears audiod-stale. In the test sandbox with the real CMake on a two-target project, an edit to the other target's source left field-audiod unlinked by the rebuild. status then printed audiod-current, and with this line removed it still printed audiod-stale.
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and the 15-second low-speed limit bound a stalled HTTPS fetch. Neither applies to an SSH remote.

Every target checks before its first command. In the test sandbox, all without cmake, without the global bin directory on PATH, without a global bin directory, or with Node 22, and audiod without cmake, each exit 69 with no install, build, or link logged.

groups.title: Workers: field setup --existing and --check
groups.kicker: The CLI, which owns the list of workers, says which are set up and whether each is current.
intro: Field's model workers are Python packages under python/<worker>/, each with an environment in .venv that uv manages. Setting one up is explicit, because the first field generate of each kind downloads that model's weights: about 10 GB for ACE-Step and 2 GB for Chatterbox. A worker counts as set up when its console script is installed in .venv/bin. A .venv alone does not count, because a dev-only uv sync creates one with no worker in it.

--existing re-syncs only the workers already set up, and prints a skipping line for each of the others. --check prints one row per worker in the installer's row format and changes nothing. It exits 1 only when a worker someone set up is out of date, or uv is missing, because a worker nobody set up is not a problem.

checks.text: partitionExisting decides with workerScriptInstalled, the same check probeEnvironment makes before field generate starts a worker. src/workers/setup.test.ts covers the installed and dev-only layouts and passed at this head.

checkWorkers pads each label to 14 characters to match row in install.sh, which passes these rows through and marks worker-stale and worker-no-uv as warnings. The probe it calls runs only uv --version and uv sync --check --locked, which change nothing.

groups.title: field upgrade and the command surface
groups.kicker: A small command that finds the install.sh beside its own package and hands it the target.
intro: Because field is a pnpm link, Node loads it from the checkout itself. So installerPath() finds install.sh two directories above dist/commands/upgrade.js, with no record of where Field was installed from. upgrade prints the command it runs, runs it through bash rather than the script's execute bit, and returns the script's exit status.
On Windows the installer does not run, so field upgrade refuses and names the steps to run in the checkout instead. src/cli.ts registers the command and the two new field setup options.

files.note: The whole command: refuse on Windows, find the installer, print the command, run it through bash, and return its status.

checks.text: The Windows refusal comes first, so field upgrade status refuses there too.

files.note: Registers field upgrade and the --existing and --check options on field setup, and names BUILD_DAEMON in three field play messages.

checks.text: --check with --existing is refused, since one reports and the other syncs.

groups.title: Daemon error messages name one build command
groups.kicker: BUILD_DAEMON replaces pnpm build:native in the eight messages that fire when field-audiod is not built.
intro: When field-audiod is not built, eight messages tell you how to build it. They fire while you work in a song project, where pnpm build:native is not a script. Each now names BUILD_DAEMON from src/audiod/client.ts, which is field upgrade audiod, a command that works from any directory. On Windows it is pnpm build:native in the Field checkout, because field upgrade refuses there.

checks.text: On Windows the value reads pnpm build:native in the field checkout, an instruction rather than a command, so every message names it outside a code span.

files.note: The field --version remedy for a daemon on the wrong protocol names BUILD_DAEMON.

groups.title: gen:limits writes the header only when it changes
groups.kicker: A generated header stops making the daemon look stale after every test run.
intro: native/audiod/src/plan-limits.h carries the zod schemas' limits into the daemon's C++, and src/schema/plan-limits.test.ts regenerates it on every pnpm test to prove it is in step. Rewriting identical bytes moved the file's modification time. That made the next daemon build recompile every file that includes the header, and made the new audiod-stale row fire after every test run.

files.note: Compares the new header with the file on disk and writes only when they differ.

checks.text: At this head, pnpm gen:limits printed is current and left the header's modification time unchanged, and src/schema/plan-limits.test.ts passed.

groups.title: Tests run the real script in a sandbox
groups.kicker: The installer's tests run install.sh under real bash with stand-ins for pnpm, cmake, and the CLI.
intro: src/install.test.ts runs the real install.sh with the machine's bash against a temporary clone that has its own upstream. pnpm and cmake are stand-ins that record their arguments, the CLI is a stand-in script, and PATH and HOME point only into the temporary directory, so the machine's real tools cannot answer in their place. src/commands/upgrade.test.ts runs bash against a stand-in installer. Both skip on Windows.

checks.text: At this head, pnpm typecheck was clean and these three files, with the generate, version, and plan-limits tests, passed: 6 files and 114 tests. On CI, linux passed and windows failed only in test files this pull request does not change.
The refusal tests now assert that a failed check logs no install, build, or link at all, through changes, rather than only that pnpm add did not run.
The pnpm stand-in leaves an existing daemon alone, as CMake does after an edit to another target's source, so this test fails without the touch in install_audiod.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: A new install guide, and every install instruction now leads with ./install.sh.
intro: docs/install.md is new. It describes the prerequisites, what each target runs, the link, worker environments, every status row, and the manual steps on Windows. The README, the CLI manual, the keys guide, and the example project's README now lead with ./install.sh and name field upgrade audiod for the daemon.

files.note: The install guide: targets, the link, workers, and the status rows.

checks.text: Review thread, P2: this paragraph says the installer checks each listed prerequisite before it changes anything, including CMake 3.24 or newer, a compiler, and the Linux headers. require_cmake checks only that cmake is on PATH, so with Ubuntu 22.04's CMake 3.22 the CLI is installed and linked before the daemon build fails. The proposed fix checks the version in require_cmake and says the build reports a missing compiler or headers.
The row now says why the installer touches the binary after each build.

files.note: The install section, the field setup options, the reference table, and FIELD_OFFLINE.

groups.title: The install plan

intro: docs/projects/install/readme.md is new at status: in-progress. §2 is the design this pull request builds, §3 sketches chunks 2 to 4, §4 records why each choice beat its alternatives, and §8 records what implementation settled and how it was verified.

§7 holds the open questions. Each must be answered or deferred to where it gets decided, because in-progress claims the plan is ready to execute. §7.1, §7.5, and the install.ps1 question in §7.6 name the chunk that decides them, and §8.3 defers the rest that gate chunks 2 to 4.
